userStories.notes: Seed story completed. userStories.title: Add config-driven cookies_from_browser field to DownloadConfig with validation
acceptanceCriteria: DownloadConfig in src/config/sections/download.py has a cookies_from_browser field (str, default 'firefox') and a cookies_path field (str, default '')
config.yaml download section documents both fields with comments explaining browser vs file cookie sources
__post_init__ validates cookies_from_browser is one of ['firefox', 'chrome', 'edge', 'safari', 'opera', 'brave', ''] (empty string disables)
A unit test verifies DownloadConfig loads cookies_from_browser from config dict and validates invalid browser names raise ValueError
A unit test verifies the default config round-trips through YAML load/dump without losing cookie fields
userStories.notes: Tier: P0 foundation. COMPLETED: Fields cookies_from_browser (str, default '') and cookies_path (str, default '') already existed in DownloadConfig at lines 1096-1097. config.yaml already documents both fields at lines 916-930. Added __post_init__ validation in DownloadConfig that rejects invalid browser names with ValueError. Added 20 tests in test_config_section_validation.py: 7 valid browsers, 7 invalid browsers, dict loading, defaults, and 3 YAML round-trip tests. All 20 tests pass. Note: Python default is '' (disabled) while config.yaml sets 'firefox' for actual usage — this matches the existing pattern where empty=disabled.

userStories.title: Fix ImpersonateTarget type conversion with case normalization in _apply_escalation_to_ydl_opts
acceptanceCriteria: _apply_escalation_to_ydl_opts in src/stages/download_segments.py converts impersonate string to ImpersonateTarget object using from_str() with lowercased client and os fields
If ImpersonateTarget import fails (yt-dlp version mismatch), the function logs a warning and omits impersonation from ydl_opts instead of crashing
A unit test verifies 'Chrome-136:Macos-15' is converted to ImpersonateTarget with client='chrome-136' and os='macos-15'
A unit test verifies that when ImpersonateTarget is unavailable (mocked ImportError), the function returns ydl_opts without the impersonate key
A unit test verifies mixed-case strings like 'FIREFOX-130:WINDOWS-11' are properly lowercased
userStories.notes: Complete. Split except Exception into ImportError (logs warning, skips impersonation) + general Exception. Added 3 tests: test_apply_escalation_import_error_logs_warning_and_omits_impersonate, test_apply_escalation_mixed_case_firefox_lowercased, test_apply_escalation_chrome_136_macos_15_conversion. All 91 download_segments tests pass.

userStories.title: Fix iterative_match video_file serialization to drill into primary_match.video_segment.source_file
acceptanceCriteria: In src/stages/iterative_match.py, the match serialization path for MatchResult objects extracts video_file from match.primary_match.video_segment.source_file instead of getattr(match, 'video_file', '')
When primary_match or video_segment is None, the code falls back to empty string without raising an exception
A unit test creates a MatchResult with a nested primary_match.video_segment.source_file='test_video.mp4' and verifies serialization produces the correct video_file value
A unit test verifies that serialized matches with non-empty video_file survive round-trip through Match.from_dict() without being rejected
A unit test verifies the fallback when primary_match is None returns empty string
userStories.notes: Complete. The serialization code at iterative_match.py:426-449 already correctly drills into primary_match.video_segment.source_file (previously fixed in US-48-003). Added 3 focused unit tests in TestVideoFileSerializationDrillDown: test_serialization_extracts_nested_source_file (source_file='test_video.mp4'), test_round_trip_through_match_from_dict (verifies Match.from_dict() accepts the serialized output), test_fallback_when_primary_match_is_none (verifies empty string fallback). All 35 match serialization tests pass.

userStories.title: Add process-level stall detection timeout around ydl.download() with configurable threshold
acceptanceCriteria: The ydl.download() call in src/stages/download_segments.py is wrapped in a ThreadPoolExecutor with a configurable timeout (default 300 seconds)
The timeout value is read from download config as segment_stall_timeout with a sensible default
When timeout fires, the download is cancelled and a DownloadStallError (or similar) is raised that feeds into the existing retry/escalation logic
A unit test verifies that a mocked ydl.download() that blocks indefinitely is killed after the timeout
A unit test verifies the timeout value is configurable through the download config section
A unit test verifies that stall timeout errors increment the retry counter and trigger escalation
userStories.notes: Tier: P1 reliability. Implementation pre-existed at download_segments.py:639-670 (US-49-004). ThreadPoolExecutor wraps ydl.download() with segment_stall_timeout (default 120s, config field at download.py:1192, config.yaml:1347). TimeoutError is caught by except Exception handler, classified as 'timeout' category, increments stats['failed'], and feeds into retry queue. Added 2 new tests: test_stall_timeout_increments_failure_and_feeds_retry_queue (AC6 - verifies failure counter, timeout classification, retry queue add) and test_stall_timeout_error_does_not_trigger_bot_escalation (verifies stalls don't trigger bot-detection escalation). All 6 TestSegmentStallTimeout tests pass.

userStories.title: Add global bot-detection counter with tier floor propagation across all video downloads
acceptanceCriteria: A stage-level consecutive_bot_detections counter in download_segments.py increments on every bot-detection error regardless of video_id

When consecutive_bot_detections exceeds BOT_DETECTION_ABORT_THRESHOLD (configurable, default 10), the stage sets a tier floor via escalation_manager.set_tier_floor() so subsequent downloads start at the highest tier
Bot-detection errors do NOT reset the network failure counter — they are counted separately from network failures
A unit test verifies that after N consecutive bot-detection errors across different video IDs, the tier floor is set to VPN_ROTATION tier
A unit test verifies that a successful download resets the consecutive bot-detection counter to zero
A unit test verifies that bot-detection errors no longer reset the network failure counter
userStories.notes: Tier: P2 resilience. Implementation pre-existed in download_segments.py (US-49-005/US-49-008). Stage-level counter at line 458, increments at line 726, tier floor set at lines 727-738 via set_tier_floor(VPN_ROTATION), abort at lines 740-772, success reset at lines 524-528/691-694, network counter isolation at lines 775-801. Added 5 tests in tests/test_bot_detection_global_counter.py: TestTierFloorPropagation (3 tests: threshold triggers set_tier_floor, below threshold no call, different video_ids prove stage-level), TestBotCounterResetOnSuccess (1 test: success resets counter and clears tier floor, second batch re-triggers), TestBotErrorsDoNotResetNetworkCounter (1 test: bot error between network errors preserves counter for abort). All 5 tests pass.

userStories.title: Expand _is_network_failure() patterns to cover Python API exception format and Windows DNS errors
acceptanceCriteria: _is_network_failure() in src/stages/download_segments.py matches Python API DownloadError messages containing 'Errno 11001' (Windows DNS resolution failure)
_is_network_failure() matches the unsigned ffmpeg exit code 4294967158 (0xFFFFFEC6, signed -314) as a network failure
_is_network_failure() matches Python API exceptions wrapped as 'DownloadError: ERROR: [youtube] ... unable to download webpage' format
A unit test for each new pattern verifies _is_network_failure() returns True
A unit test verifies existing patterns (connection refused, timeout) still match after changes
userStories.notes: Pre-implemented in US-49-006. All patterns already in _NETWORK_FAILURE_PATTERNS (Errno 11001, URLError, ConnectionResetError, ffmpeg exit code 4294967158). 16 tests in TestIsNetworkFailurePythonApiFormat + 1 in TestNetworkFailureCircuitBreaker all pass. No code changes needed.

userStories.title: Wire circuit breaker into download_segments stage with escalation manager coordination
acceptanceCriteria: The download_segments stage creates a CircuitBreaker instance and wires it to the EscalationManager via set_circuit_breaker() before the download loop begins
When the circuit breaker trips (is_open), downloads are paused using check_and_wait() instead of immediately failing
Circuit breaker state is included in the stage metrics written to checkpoint (total_trips, total_paused_seconds)
A unit test verifies that CircuitBreaker is instantiated and linked to EscalationManager
A unit test verifies that when circuit breaker is open, the download loop calls check_and_wait() and respects the pause duration
userStories.notes: Tier: P2 integration. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py (circuit breaker check at lines 521-548, wiring at line 474), src/downloader/circuit_breaker.py (CircuitBreaker class, check_and_wait at lines 294-340), src/downloader/escalation_manager.py (set_circuit_breaker at lines 291-300). Exploration shows circuit breaker is already wired at line 474 and checked at lines 521-548. This story adds tests and ensures metrics flow to checkpoint.

userStories.title: Add integration test for download_segments cookie propagation with mocked yt-dlp
acceptanceCriteria: An integration test creates a DownloadConfig with cookies_from_browser='firefox' and verifies the ydl_opts dict passed to YoutubeDL contains cookiesfrombrowser=['firefox']
An integration test creates a DownloadConfig with cookies_path='/path/to/cookies.txt' and no cookies_from_browser, and verifies ydl_opts contains cookiefile='/path/to/cookies.txt'
An integration test verifies that when both cookies_from_browser and cookies_path are set, cookies_from_browser takes priority
An integration test verifies that when neither is set, ydl_opts contains neither cookiesfrombrowser nor cookiefile keys
All tests mock YoutubeDL to avoid actual network calls
userStories.notes: Tier: P0 validation. Source file: src/stages/download_segments.py (cookie handling at lines 579-595). This validates the cookie propagation added in sprint 49. The ydl_opts construction at lines 565-596 should set cookiesfrombrowser as a list (yt-dlp Python API expects [browser_name]) not a string. Test file: tests/test_download_segments_cookies.py (new).

userStories.title: Add retry queue tier persistence so retried downloads start at their last escalation tier
acceptanceCriteria: When a download fails and is queued for retry, the current escalation tier is stored with the retry entry
When retrying, the download starts at the stored tier (or the global tier floor, whichever is higher) instead of Tier 1
A unit test verifies that a video that failed at Tier 2 starts its retry at Tier 2 (not Tier 1)
A unit test verifies that if the global tier floor is Tier 3 and the stored retry tier is Tier 2, the retry starts at Tier 3
A unit test verifies that videos with no stored tier (legacy retry entries) default to Tier 1
userStories.notes: Tier: P2 efficiency. Source file: src/stages/download_segments.py. The retry queue at the stage level re-enqueues failed video IDs but doesn't persist escalation state. Each retry restarts at Tier 1, wasting time re-escalating through tiers that already failed. The EscalationManager tracks per-keyword tier state internally — check if keyword_id maps to video_id and if state persists across the retry pass. Sprint 49 story US-49-010 added tier persistence across passes — verify integration.

userStories.title: Add download config validation that warns when no cookie source is configured
acceptanceCriteria: During pipeline startup (or download_segments stage init), if neither cookies_from_browser nor cookies_path is configured, a WARNING log is emitted explaining that YouTube will likely block all requests
The warning includes actionable guidance: 'Set download.cookies_from_browser to your browser name (firefox, chrome, etc.) in config.yaml'
If cookies_from_browser is set to a browser not installed on the system, a WARNING is logged (best-effort check, not a hard error)
A unit test verifies the warning is emitted when no cookie config is present
A unit test verifies no warning when cookies_from_browser is properly configured
userStories.notes: Tier: P1 UX/safety. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py (stage init or _build_ydl_opts), src/config/sections/download.py. This provides early feedback to users about missing cookies — the #1 cause of bot-detection failures. The validation should happen early (stage init, not per-download) to avoid log spam. Could also check if the browser cookie extraction actually works by attempting a dry-run import.
